headline: Solar incentives in New Jersey in 2026
summary: Homeowners who assume solar is dead without the federal tax credit haven't looked at New Jersey's state programs. NJ still combines strong production incentives, sales/property tax treatment, and (for now) full retail net metering on IOUs — confirm current BPU rates.
net_metering_or_billing_overview: New Jersey has historically mandated full 1:1 retail-rate net metering for residential solar on investor-owned utilities. Always confirm the current BPU rule and your utility’s interconnection package.

programs.name: Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) ADI Program
programs.summary: The ADI program replaced the volatile SREC market with a fixed multi-year payment for energy produced. Research notes a residential rate of $77.00 per MWh ($0.077/kWh) for registrations on or after July 27, 2026 — verify on the official NJ Clean Energy page before modeling.
programs.dollar_amounts: Research cited $77.00/MWh fixed for 15 years for late-2026 registrations — confirm official tracker.
programs.stacking_notes: Often stacks with net metering and NJ sales tax exemption.

programs.name: Solar Equipment Sales Tax Exemption
programs.summary: Solar energy systems and related equipment are generally exempt from New Jersey state sales and use tax when qualifying — confirm with your installer invoice.
programs.dollar_amounts: State sales tax avoided at point of sale when exemption applies.

property_tax_sales_tax_notes: New Jersey generally excludes qualifying solar from property tax assessment increases — confirm current statute with local assessor.
hoa_solar_access_law: New Jersey limits HOA powers to ban solar; aesthetic restrictions may still apply. Read current statute before fighting an architectural board.

sections.heading: Understanding SuSI ADI value in 2026
sections.body: Under SuSI ADI (often called SREC-II by installers), the state framework pays for generating clean electricity. Rates are administratively set and can change by registration date. Ask whether your installer will assign/sell the incentive stream upfront or leave quarterly payments with you.

faqs.question: Do I have to sell my SRECs myself?
faqs.answer: Under SuSI ADI, installers or aggregators usually handle registration. Ask who owns the incentive stream if they offer an upfront buyout.
